name: University of Hertfordshire

settingEvidence.evidence: The University has two main, easy-to-reach and accessible campuses – College Lane and de Havilland – both based in Hatfield and well-connected for travel around Hertfordshire and into central London.

fees.text: £10,050 per year for UK students on full-time courses starting in 2027 (2027/28). Herts says tuition fees are charged annually and may be higher in future years.

livingCosts.text: On-campus halls cost about £134–£289 a week in 2026/27 depending on the room and contract length (twin en suite from £134.12 per person; single £159.74–£165.97; single en suite at de Havilland, where these courses are taught, £204.26–£243.95; studio en suite up to £289.10). Electricity, gas, water and internet are included in the rent.

openDays.text: Next undergraduate open day: Saturday 21 November 2026, 09:30-15:00 (College Lane Campus). 2027 dates not announced yet.

contextual.summary: UK (Home fee) applicants who meet at least one of Herts' criteria are considered automatically for a contextual offer, typically up to one grade lower (about eight UCAS points).
contextual.typicalReduction: Typically up to one grade lower than the standard entry requirements (equivalent to eight UCAS points)

criteria.detail: You received free school meals at any point in the last six years during secondary education.
You were in care before the age of 16.
You care, unpaid, for a friend or family member with an illness or disability, mental health condition or an addiction.
You are irreconcilably estranged from both parents and receive no support from them.
You are a Home fee applicant with refugee status.
Your home postcode (from your UCAS form) falls into IMD Quintile 1, the areas facing the most significant socioeconomic challenges (IMD decile 1-2).
Gypsy, Roma, Traveller, Showmen and Boater applicants: email the Student Success team with your full name and UCAS number to be considered for a contextual offer.

contextual.rulesText: To be considered, you must be a UK domiciled student with Home fee status and meet at least one of the criteria. If you meet them, the admissions team considers you for a contextual offer automatically. Grade adjustments are not available for part-time applicants, deferred entry or Clearing, and for some courses adjustments may not be possible.

source.evidence: A contextual offer is typically up to one grade lower than our standard entry requirements (equivalent to eight UCAS points).
